author: Helen Hunt Jackson
title: A Calendar of Sonnets
edition: Boston: Roberts Brothers, 1891, Harvard University copy at Internet Archive acalendarsonnet01jackgoog; the printed title page reads 1891 although the catalogue uses copyright 1886. Gutenberg 9825 does not identify its print exemplar: every line of all 12 selected poems was therefore collated against this dated primary witness. The chosen words and punctuation match; Gutenberg plain-text straight apostrophes, double-hyphen em dashes, flattened small-cap openings and indentation are retained, with trailing whitespace removed. July has 13 printed lines in the witness; none are supplied or omitted. Publisher and digitizer matter and illustrations are excluded. The library text holds all twelve sonnets under their month headings. In August, “middle-agèd” takes its grave accent from the HTML file of the same Gutenberg eBook; the plain-text file has “middle-aged”.

rights.basis: The original English text in this 1891 edition was published before 1931 and is public domain in the United States in 2026. The dated source and its public-domain record are linked; no modern introductions, annotations, or illustrations are reproduced.

acquisition.method: Project Gutenberg plain text (eBook 9825, UTF-8, CRLF normalised to LF) from the PG mirror. Kept the twelve month headings and sonnets; removed the PG header and footer and the transcription’s title lines (title, author, 1886). Month names are headings; each sonnet is one stanza with the transcription’s lines and two-space indentation (and the indented second half of a split line) kept, only trailing spaces removed. The files, in order: https://aleph.pglaf.org/cache/epub/9825/pg9825.txt (the download URL), then the HTML file of the same eBook, https://aleph.pglaf.org/cache/epub/9825/pg9825-images.html; the hash is of the two downloads concatenated in that order. One letter follows the HTML file, as the nightly reading has it: “middle-agèd” in August, where the plain-text file prints “middle-aged”. Converted by a scratch Node script; every nightly reading was located exactly.
